review: Practical and easy to apply, I started using habit stacking the next day.
The four laws of behaviour change are simple and memorable.
Clear writing and great real life examples, I finished it in two days.
Good ideas, but the book repeats the same points many times.
Interesting, but the stories about athletes felt a bit cherry picked.
The chapter on identity based habits changed how I think about goals.
Most of it is common sense that could have been a blog post.
The idea of getting 1 percent better every day really stuck with me.
Great value, I keep going back to my highlights.
Overhyped, I expected more science and less anecdotes.
The second half drags compared with the first.
Short chapters make it easy to read a little every night.
The paperback is well printed and the summary tables at the end are useful.
A useful book, though the ideas are not really new.
James Clear explains everything so simply, perfect for beginners.
The best self help book I've read, I recommend it to everyone.
